AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The impact of metformin on body weight is variable in T2DM patients among studies. The reasons for discrepancies are still unknown.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: We aimed to find out the possible predictive factors of weight change induced by metformin based on an analysis of a phase IV open-labeled trial.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: We performed a sub-analysis from a prospective, multi-center, Phase IV open-labeled study in which 371 Chinese newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients received 16 weeks' extended-release metformin monotherapy. The clinical characteristics including weight and laboratory assessments of subjects were collected every 4 weeks. The weight changes from baseline to week 4, 8, 12 and 16 were calculated respectively. The patients were divided into 4 groups by quartile statistic method according to magnitudes of weight change.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of 371 enrolled patients, 324 patients had the weight records from baseline to week 16. The weight decreased gradually with visit (p<0.001) and the medium weight loss was 2 kg after 16 weeks' treatment of metformin. The patients with higher BMI, and bigger waist circumference at baseline showed a more pronounced weight loss. However, the magnitudes of weight loss were independently associated with BMI at baseline only.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Metformin can lead to weight loss gradually in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients. The magnitude of weight loss was independently and only associated with baseline BMI.
